item.title: Compositionally Complex Ceramics (CCCs): A New Paradigm in Ceramics
item.description: arXiv:2608.27812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The development of high-entropy ceramics (HECs) over the past decade has extended the exploration to a diverse range of oxides, borides, silicides, carbides, nitrides, fluorides, and other ceramic solid solutions, encompassing an increasingly broad range of crystal structures and bonding characteristics and exhibiting promising mechanical, thermal, and functional properties. Initial studies predominantly focused on five-component equimolar compositions. In 2020, we proposed extending the exploration beyond HECs to the broader class of "compositionally complex ceramics" (CCCs), in which rational non-equimolar compositional designs and long- and short-range order can reduce configurational entropy while providing additional opportunities to tailor and enhance materials properties, with the goal of outperforming their higher-entropy counterparts. Because CCCs have been defined somewhat vaguely in previous publications, this review seeks to establish more rigorous and explicit criteria for defining CCCs, despite the unavoidable degree of arbitrariness in the choice of thresholds. Meanwhile, 10-21-component ultrahigh-entropy ceramics have emerged as a subset of HECs, exhibiting intriguing abrupt phase transitions. Dual-phase CCCs have also been reported, with thermodynamic equilibria governing cation partitioning between the two phases. Recent studies have further revealed that grain-boundary complexion (phase-like) transitions can occur in CCCs, influencing microstructural evolution and materials properties. Overall, CCCs provide a versatile platform for tailoring materials properties through the interplay of diverse crystal structures and bonding characteristics, compositional complexity, rational non-equimolar designs, long- and short-range order, defects, and microstructural and interfacial engineering.

item.title: Tunable anisotropy of high-harmonic generation in ferroelectric NbOI2
item.description: arXiv:2610.24302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The generation of even-order harmonic spectra from inversion symmetry breaking is well known, however, the tunability of the intensity and angular anisotropy on various harmonics orders remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the second and fourth-harmonics in the ferroelectric NbOI2 exhibit distinct wavelength-dependence and anisotropies in the near-infrared regime. In particular, as the wavelength of incident light is tuned from 2150 nm to 2450 nm, the second-harmonic remains strongest for excitation along the ferroelectric polar axis, whereas the polarization of the fourth- harmonic changes preferred axis. This effect is found to be driven by the interplay of transition dipole matrix elements and interband excitations between very narrow bands near the Fermi level. We expect the tunable anisotropy of high-harmonics to enable novel optical switching devices.

item.title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
item.description: arXiv:2610.34736v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation $\mathrm{(0.0086 \pm 0.0002) \mu_{B}/Mn}$ that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of $\mathrm{(291 \pm 2)\, K}$.

item.title: Generation and spectroscopic characterization of continuous-wave 148.4-nm light in strontium tetraborate
item.description: arXiv:2610.42055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous-wave (CW) radiation at 148.4~nm is required to drive the $^{229}$Th isomeric transition of a solid-state nuclear clock, and frequency doubling of 296.8-nm light is its most direct source. We generate CW 148.4-nm light by random quasi-phase matching in strontium tetraborate and characterize it with a compact CaF$_2$ prism spectrometer, which reaches picowatt sensitivity without filters or a grating and reads the wavelength from the rotation angle of a solar-blind photomultiplier. The observed harmonic profile has an angular FWHM of 0.36$^{\circ}$, corresponding to a convolution-limited spectral width of about 0.6 nm rather than the intrinsic linewidth. The directly estimated output is 1.9 nW at room temperature; scaling the measured temperature dependence gives an inferred 4.8 nW at the best observed temperature. The conversion varies by an order of magnitude across the crystal and is strongly structured in temperature: between 30 $^{\circ}$C and 50 $^{\circ}$C it shows several maxima only a few degrees apart, so a small excursion moves the output from a maximum to a minimum. These measurements provide valuable information on the realization and characterization of a high-quality 148.4-nm light source, and pave the way for the future development of high-performance nuclear optical clocks.

item.title: Intrinsic non-Markovian magnetisation dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2512.07378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Memory effects are widespread in complex systems while evidence of non-Markovian dynamics in fundamental physical systems has been limited to specifically engineered cases. Here we report on the experimental observation of non-Markovian magnetisation dynamics in crystalline cobalt. Intense terahertz electromagnetic driving brings the system into a non-equilibrium state, and allows us to follow its magnetisation dynamics in real time at low temperatures. The response reveals a striking multi-peaked frequency spectrum that defies conventional descriptions. Using open quantum system theory we evidence that a non-Markovian memory kernel, arising from spin-phonon bath coupling, naturally explains both the spectral structure and its temperature dependence. Theoretical prediction of the spectrum is accomplished by simulating the non-Markovian Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, while analytics quantitatively determines the frequencies of three spectral peaks. The results demonstrate that intrinsic memory effects can emerge in a simple ferromagnet, opening new opportunities to explore and control non-Markovian dynamics in condensed-matter systems.

item.title: Disentangling Spin Pumping and Two-Magnon Scattering Contributions to Gilbert Damping in YIG/V Bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2605.29597v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the magnetic damping and spin pumping response of YIG-based bilayers incorporating vanadium (V) as the normal metal layer via broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurements as a function of YIG thickness. We show that the apparent enhancement of the Gilbert damping in YIG/V bilayers cannot be solely attributed to spin pumping. Instead, two-magnon scattering (TMS) plays a dominant role in governing the thickness dependence of the damping in the nanometer regime. By applying a thickness-dependent damping model that accounts for both spin pumping and two-magnon scattering contributions, we successfully disentangle the different relaxation contributions. Our analysis reveals that neglecting two-magnon scattering leads to an overestimation of the spin-pumping contribution and consequently to unphysically large values of the effective spin-mixing conductance. After isolating the intrinsic spin pumping contribution, we extract a thickness-independent effective spin-mixing conductance of $g^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.33 \times 10^{18}~\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These findings provide a more accurate framework for quantifying spin transport parameters in FM/HM systems and emphasize the necessity of accounting for extrinsic damping mechanisms when interpreting spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect experiments.
